bullets: Game 3 of 6 of this single-deck session (video 339.2s-629.0s); won against a Goblin Giant / Elite Barbarians / Sparky beatdown deck with a Skeleton King tower troop — "GG's. Very nice win" (t=622-624). Enemy left tower 4858 -> 682; his own towers finished 4632 and 4858.

Same shell as X-Bow HeroKnight 3.0 Cycle (decks/archers-electro-spirit-fireball-knight-skeletons-tesla-the-log-x-bow.md) with the Hero Berserker in the Knight slot; Evolutions in play are Archers and Tesla.

Stated game plan against beatdown (t=389-400): "all we have to do is just keep on doing light pressure, defend, and just keep going in and he's never really able to build up a proper attack. It is really complicated for him to actually go in for a really big push as long as I play it right."

Standard offensive unit: split Evo Archers at [8, 0] (t=350, 398, 445, 572) plus a bridge Berserker (with ability) in front of an X-Bow at [4, 12]/[4, 13] — "I just love going X-Bow with the Evo Archers down the middle" (t=447-450). That loop took the enemy left tower 4708 -> 1964 between clock 0:34 and 0:08.

Defence is Evo Tesla in the middle of his own half ([8, 10]/[8, 12], t=416, 451, 489, 544) supported by 1-elixir Electro Spirit and Skeletons, with The Log for resets; Fireball was held for overtime only and spent on Electro Wizard, Rage and Sparky.

The Hero Berserker is the flex slot: emergency defence when caught off guard (t=355-360), X-Bow tank at the bridge (t=476-479), and Elite Barbarians cleanup — "just having the Berserker plus ability to clean up the e-barbs behind any type of push is just super nice" (t=608-610).

The named failure mode of the deck is over-attacking: "the biggest mistake I find people making with expo is just not knowing when to just quit attacking... You have to have some really, really good defense to save doing a bad expo against these types of beatdown decks" (t=544-565). He acts on it at overtime 0:52 by cycling Archers instead of laying another X-Bow.

new_deck.rationale: The X-Bow is the only win condition and every other card is a cheap defensive or cycle piece that exists to get back to it.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: It is the standard 3.0 X-Bow cycle shell — Evo Archers, Evo Tesla, Electro Spirit, Skeletons, The Log, Fireball — with the Hero Berserker replacing the Knight as the 2-elixir tank. The Berserker is cheaper than a Knight, so the cycle back to the X-Bow is faster, and its 3-elixir "Savage Survival" ability turns it into a burst troop-clearer that answers the cards this shell normally struggles with: Elite Barbarians behind a tank, a Goblin Giant at the bridge, and a Sparky shot it can soak without dying. On offence the pattern is split Evo Archers at the back, a bridge Berserker, then the X-Bow one row off the river, recycling each defence into the next attack. The deck wins by chip, not by a single push — "all it takes is that one lock" — so the discipline is knowing when to hold the X-Bow and set up an Evo Tesla in the middle instead.
